subject: Copywriting
title: Pepsi: Come Alive
description: A quick, practical guide to Pepsi: Come Alive.

hook.text: 'Come Alive with the Pepsi Generation' sounded great in English.

buildup.text: The 1960s slogan aimed at youth energy. It worked in Western markets. International rollout was not tested locally.

discovery.text: The mistranslation story—possibly apocryphal—became a legendary cautionary tale taught in every advertising course.

twist.text: Even if the exact translation is debated, the principle is real: dozens of brands have suffered genuine translation.

climax.text: The lesson became standard practice: test slogans in every target market with native speakers before global launch.

punchline.text: Test locally or die globally. Translation disasters are preventable.

quiz.question: What lesson did Pepsi's translation issue teach?
options: Always test slogans with native speakers in target markets

details.summary: Pepsi's 'Come Alive! You're in the Pepsi Generation' targeted young consumers in the 1960s, but its global rollout hit a notorious snag. In Chinese markets, the slogan was reportedly translated as 'Pepsi brings your ancestors back from the grave' — a famous cautionary tale about cross-cultural...
details.whyItMatters: The Pepsi translation legend — whether fully accurate or embellished — highlights the very real danger of deploying slogans across cultures without local expertise. It made transcreation a standard practice.
takeaways: The English slogan successfully targeted youth culture in the 1960s
Cross-cultural translation produced an unintended macabre meaning
The incident popularized transcreation as a professional discipline

faq.question: Did the Chinese mistranslation really happen?
faq.answer: The exact details are debated — some scholars call it an urban legend, others confirm a version of the mistranslation. Regardless, it became the most cited example in marketing textbooks for why literal translation fails in global advertising.

faq.question: What was the original intent of 'Come Alive with Pepsi'?
faq.answer: The slogan targeted Baby Boomers as the 'Pepsi Generation,' positioning Pepsi as the young, energetic alternative to Coca-Cola. In English, 'come alive' clearly meant feeling energized and vibrant — a meaning that didn't translate universally.
